intent.note: Clause: 'Pass the interpreter in a form the shell can execute ... or skip only on the platform's own probe ... never reading any exception as the platform refusing. Keep the case running on posix; add a posix case that proves the conversion is applied.' The diff adds shell_spelled (separator swap to '/') and routes _run_live_window's LW_PY through it (default sep=os.sep, so lw1 on posix is unchanged and on Windows now gets C:/... form). lw4 pins the conversion on any OS, lw5 runs the step with a Windows-shaped interpreter via a stand-in at a relative C:/... path, and lw5 is skipped only when os.path.splitdrive reads 'C:' as a drive, which is the platform's own path probe and not an exception. No try/except swallows anything; a missing POSIX shell stays a red check. The executor's outcome describes the diff accurately: only tools/gate-parity.py changed and the listed dependants (verify.sh's _live_window_cases, ci.yml etc.) are untouched in contract. One nuance: the task says 'as verify.sh's own runner does on Windows', but verify.sh's own runner uses `python3() { python "$@"; }` and `cygpath -m` only for a project path, not for the interpreter. The executor's claim that the fix is the existing mechanism holds for the tests/ suites, which spell sys.executable.replace('\\','/') for Git Bash (tests/test_drive_phase.py:1127, tests/test_stamp_verification.py:4604, among others). It is the same mechanism with a name, not a second one. The Windows outcome itself is unverified here and the executor says so (owner to confirm on Windows).
